title: Diffusion model
reading: The slide introduces diffusion models by analogy to autoregressive models run in reverse: beginning from a complete image, pixels are removed one after another, a process described as signal corruption. It then states that a diffusion model adds noise to produce a progressively noisier signal, and notes that the noise used is most commonly isotropic Gaussian noise.

concepts.name: Diffusion model
concepts.why_it_matters: Framed as progressive corruption of a signal by added noise, the basis of the generative process.

concepts.name: Signal corruption
concepts.why_it_matters: The forward destruction process that diffusion later learns to reverse.

concepts.name: Isotropic Gaussian noise
concepts.why_it_matters: The standard noise choice that makes the forward process tractable.

concepts.name: Autoregressive model
concepts.why_it_matters: Used as the comparison point for understanding diffusion as its reverse.
